skill.name: m365-agents-py
skill.description: Guides implementation of Microsoft 365 Agents SDK for Python agents, including aiohttp hosting, routing, streaming, OAuth, and Copilot Studio integration.
skill.summary: Build Microsoft 365, Teams, and Copilot Studio agents with Python SDK patterns.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown fences, inline backticks, static Python imports, placeholders, and reference links. Confirmed risks are limited to low-severity dotenv and authenticated Microsoft Graph examples, with a medium semantic concern around broad OAuth .default scope usage. No prompt-injection attempt or malicious data-exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: The Copilot Studio example uses the Power Platform .default OAuth scope.
remediation.suggestion: Document the exact permissions required, avoid .default where narrower scopes are available, and require tenant consent review before production use.

remediation.issue: The examples load secrets from .env and environment variables.
remediation.suggestion: Add explicit guidance to keep .env files out of source control, rotate leaked credentials, and use managed secret stores in production.

remediation.issue: The Microsoft Graph example returns profile data into the chat conversation.
remediation.suggestion: Minimize returned fields, confirm user consent, and warn developers not to log tokens or unnecessary profile data.

semantic_findings.title: Broad OAuth Default Scope in Copilot Studio Example
semantic_findings.description: The Copilot Studio token request uses the Power Platform .default scope, which can request all pre-consented permissions for that resource. Production guidance should narrow or explicitly justify scopes.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The exact .default scope is present in the token request, and broad default scopes are a known permission-governance risk. The surrounding code is legitimate, so severity is medium rather than high.

semantic_findings.title: Authenticated Profile Data Returned to Chat
semantic_findings.description: The Graph profile example retrieves signed-in user data and sends the display name back into the conversation. This may expose profile data in chat transcripts if copied without data-minimization review.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The sample directly obtains a user token, calls the Graph profile endpoint, and sends displayName to chat. It is expected behavior but still creates a privacy review requirement.

content.value_statement: Teams and Copilot Studio agent projects require accurate SDK patterns, routing, streaming, and authentication setup. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code focused Python guidance for Microsoft 365 Agents SDK implementations.
actual_capabilities: Scaffolds aiohttp-hosted AgentApplication patterns for Microsoft 365 agents.
Shows message, invoke, conversation update, fallback, and error routing patterns.
Guides MSAL authentication setup with CloudAdapter and Authorization components.
Demonstrates streaming responses with Azure OpenAI and sensitivity labels.
Provides OAuth auto sign-in examples for Microsoft Graph profile requests.
Shows Copilot Studio client setup for direct engine conversations.
limitations: It is a guidance skill, not a runnable project template.
API signatures may change, so official Microsoft documentation must be checked.
Production storage, deployment, and tenant governance are not fully implemented.
Examples require valid Microsoft tenant, app registration, and secret configuration.

best_practices: Verify current Microsoft Agents SDK APIs before generating final implementation code.
Use environment variables or managed secret stores, and never commit tenant secrets.
Limit OAuth scopes, validate tenant configuration, and review consent before deployment.
anti_patterns: Do not copy sample `.default` scopes into production without permission review.
Do not use MemoryStorage for production conversations or user state.
Do not log OAuth tokens, profile data, or Copilot Studio conversation content.

faq.question: What does this skill help build?
faq.answer: It helps build Python agents for Microsoft 365, Teams, and Copilot Studio using Microsoft Agents SDK patterns.

faq.question: Does it create a complete production service?
faq.answer: No. It provides implementation guidance and examples that need testing, deployment work, and tenant-specific review.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists compatibility with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it require Microsoft credentials?
faq.answer: Yes. Real projects need tenant values, app registrations, OAuth settings, and secret management outside source control.

faq.question: Can it help with streaming responses?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for Azure OpenAI streaming and closing streaming responses safely.

faq.question: What should be reviewed before publishing an agent?
faq.answer: Review scopes, consent, storage, logging, tenant isolation, middleware, and current Microsoft SDK documentation.
